title: Cercospora brown leaf spot on cassava

Header: Cercospora brown leaf spot on cassava
Mycosphaerella henningsii (syn. Cercospora henningsi) Brown leaf spot

Prevention: Keep field clean by removing dead leaves and burn them because otherwise fungal disease spores will persist and spread
Avoid getting cuttings from previously infested fields to prevent spreading of the disease.
Get planting materials from a clean farmer’s field
Rotate cassava with unrelated crops, such as maize for 2 to 3 years to break the cycle of the disease
Plant with recommended spacing (usually at 1m x 1m) to allow air flow
For overgrown cassava plants, pruning will improve aeration and reduce disease development
Clean tools and personal protective gear to avoid spreading spores
Monitoring: Cercospora leaf spot is a fungal disease mainly occurring in the hot and rainy season across the country
Check for disease symptoms on cassava leaves once per month
Check for brown spots with a yellowish ring on leaves throughout the growing period of cassava.
Look for lesions that are 0.15 to 0.2cm in diameter
Consider control when 1-3 plants out of 10 plants in the field are affected.
Direct Control: Remove most affected leaves (10 to 15 spots on the leaves) from the plant to reduce spread of the disease.
Remove fallen leaves and debris from the field and burn them.
Burning is usually not preferred in
IPM, but a good option to prevent fungal spore carry over.
Carbendazim (Carbendazim, Assure, and others); a protective fungicide that inhibits mitosis and cell division.
Cannot cure, but can prevent spread of disease.
Multisite activity group of fungicide, with protective and some curative action.
Systemic fungicide with some curative action.
Restrictions: The fungicides below are toxic to fish so do not mix, spray, clean near rivers or dispose container in water bodies (at least 50m distance)
When using a pesticide, always wear protective clothing.
Follow the instructions on the product label.
If disease persists after spraying with chemical, take samples to plant doctors for further advice.

Always consult recent list of registered pesticides (ZEMA).
Interval (r.e.i.) 1 day, thus after drying of spray
